package_info.why_malicious: This package version contains a known vulnerability (CVE-2017-1000070) that allows URL redirection to untrusted sites (Open Redirect) due to improper input validation, violating security best practices and RFC-6819.

execution_context.file_location: core application logic handling OAuth redirects

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Improper input validation in redirect URL handling, allowing user-supplied URLs to be used for redirection without proper sanitization.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Allows attackers to craft URLs that redirect users to arbitrary, potentially malicious sites during the OAuth authentication process.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Redirecting users to arbitrary URLs based on untrusted input is a classic security anti-pattern and a common vector for phishing and credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal OAuth implementations should strictly validate and whitelist redirect URLs to prevent open redirects. This code fails to do so.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate redirects are used in OAuth flows, but only to pre-approved, trusted domains.
key_indicators: Lack of input validation on redirect URLs
Use of user-supplied data in HTTP redirects

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious OAuth authentication URL with a redirect parameter pointing to an attacker-controlled site.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is redirected to an untrusted site after authentication, enabling phishing or further attacks.

behavioral_signatures: OAuth flow with unvalidated or user-controlled redirect URLs
Redirects to external domains not on an allowlist
Presence of known vulnerable package versions (e.g., github.com/bitly/oauth2_proxy@<=2.1)
file_indicators: Gopkg.lock or go.sum listing github.com/bitly/oauth2_proxy@0.9 or earlier
Application code with HTTP redirects using untrusted input
network_indicators: HTTP 302/301 responses to domains outside the application's control during OAuth flows
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan dependency manifests (Gopkg.lock, go.sum) for known vulnerable versions of github.com/bitly/oauth2_proxy. Analyze application code for HTTP redirects that use user-supplied input without validation. Monitor runtime behavior for OAuth flows that redirect to non-whitelisted domains. Use SCA tools like Nancy to automate detection of known vulnerable dependencies.
